parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the pure ESM, local .mjs, manual CLI, no npm, and executable-observed Whoosh behavior requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent spawned a CLI probing child and a design/modules child while also implementing its own solution, leaving two agents able to write the final /output deliverable.
parallel.implementation: The parent produced lib/argparse.mjs, lib/pyint.mjs, lib/miniwhoosh/*, and test15.mjs; the design child separately produced lib/cli, lib/search, lib/whoosh, lib/fs, and its own test15.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After seeing the alternate child tree, the parent interrupted the child, deleted the child library files and child test15.mjs, recreated its own test15.mjs, and delivered the miniwhoosh tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran many executable and Node comparisons for argparse, fielded queries, boolean behavior, one-character tokens, and numeric ranges, but one attempted batch comparison was blocked by a command policy.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The completed evaluator marked the final artifact failed at 51/70; compared with serial, the trajectory does not show the signed 32-bit NUMERIC bound check that serial added.

serial.requirements: The single agent recognized the same pure ESM, local .mjs, manual argv, no npm, and executable-observed behavior obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With multi-agent disabled, the same agent owned probing, implementation, fixes, verification, and final delivery of the one output tree.
serial.implementation: It wrote bigint-utils, cli, fields, analyzer, query, qparser, index, tempdir, and test15.mjs in one coordinated tree, then patched CLI and analyzer behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There were no child file writes or branch merges; the final artifact validation lists one coherent /output tree with the expected test15.mjs entry.
serial.verification: The serial agent repeatedly compared Node behavior with the executable and specifically checked help/errors, content and price queries, one-character token suppression, and large numeric failure behavior.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The completed evaluator still marked the solution failed at 57/70, so its extra coverage improved but did not fully satisfy the hidden testcase set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the requested pure ESM local-module port, manual argv parser, and executable-observed query behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same requirements and also explicitly closed on signed 32-bit NUMERIC range behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirements were broadly understood in both; serial covered one additional hidden-prone numeric edge before delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across a probe child, a design child, and parent implementation, with overlapping implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial disabled multi-agent mode and kept probing, implementation, and delivery in one owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split created overlapping final-artifact ownership, while serial had no cross-agent ownership boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent sent the design child follow-up context, but there was no stable shared-file ownership boundary and the child wrote a separate /output/test15.mjs tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff boundary; the same actor retained the interface decisions and file layout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context was sufficient for child exploration, but file ownership was resolved only after the child had already produced a conflicting deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented a miniwhoosh tree and argparse helpers, while a child separately implemented cli/search/whoosh modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one broader tree with bigint helpers, parser modules, index, fields, analyzer, and the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had competing implementation paths and delivered the parent path; serial's single path incorporated later numeric-bound fixes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The probe child returned a completed result, but the design child was interrupted after writing files and before a final result was returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and closed only after its own verification and final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had one useful child result and one interrupted implementation child, while serial avoided child-result join and cancellation states.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel shared /output across parent and child, producing two module trees and a child-owned /output/test15.mjs that the parent deleted and recreated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and kept one /output tree, with artifact validation listing that single entry and library set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel had a concrete shared-state overwrite of the entry deliverable; serial had no cross-agent workspace collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran many local probes and comparisons, but one larger comparison harness was rejected and final verification stayed representative rather than exhaustive.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran representative comparisons and then probed/fixed additional numeric-bound behavior against the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed more edge cases before delivery; parallel verified many common cases but not the large NUMERIC range failure it later missed relative to serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout but used three rollouts, 313 tool calls, and over four million total tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout using one rollout, 118 tool calls, and about 1.43 million total tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed substantially more coordination and tool budget because of child activity and cleanup, but not enough evidence shows budget exhaustion as the failure mode.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both_fail pair, not a discordant outcome: parallel failed 51/70 and serial failed 57/70. The serial trajectory shows better edge coverage, especially signed 32-bit NUMERIC bounds, while the parallel trajectory shows a concrete deliverable overwrite/reconciliation episode. The overwrite is an adverse parallel coordination event, but it is not proven to explain an outcome difference because both artifacts still failed.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had competing parent and child implementation trees and deleted a child-written /output/test15.mjs before finalizing the parent deliverable.
Parallel's final artifact and trajectory do not show the large signed 32-bit NUMERIC range behavior that serial later identified.
serial_contributors: Serial kept a single implementation path and added a signed 32-bit NUMERIC range check after comparing a large integer case against the executable.
Serial verified one-character token suppression and fielded query behavior before final delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations remained incomplete relative to hidden evaluator cases; the observed score gap is better explained by ordinary edge-case coverage plus the parallel cleanup episode than by a discordant pass/fail root cause.
evaluator_effects: No per-testcase hidden failure details are present in the accessible pair data, so the official score gap cannot be decomposed beyond the observed trajectory evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported comparative process and coverage differences only

candidates.reason: Implementation had active owners: the parent wrote a miniwhoosh tree and the design child separately wrote another implementation.
The parent owned reconciliation by inspecting /output, deleting the child tree, and continuing with its own implementation.
Both parent and child wrote an entry file and the final artifact validation found test15.mjs, so assembly was not ownerless.
The parent managed the end-to-end path from probes through edits, cleanup, verification, and final response.
The parent probed and implemented while the design child was active; implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
Parallel investigation and implementation overlapped; the parent began writing modules before the design child finished.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved; the parent actively implemented and delivered while children ran.
Only two children were spawned, the run did not time out, and no collective fan-out exhaustion displaced final delivery.
The design child scope was broad, but it produced files; the adverse event was the later shared deliverable overwrite, not unfinished scope from oversizing.
The child trajectory included the full task prompt and pursued CLI and Whoosh behavior; no known requirement omission in a child brief is visible.
The agents did diverge on workspace paths, but the concrete realized event was deletion and replacement of the entry deliverable, which is the more specific write label.
The probe child returned a concise result and the parent used probe findings; no known information disappeared through transfer.
No returned handoff was too bulky to consume; the problematic design-child work was a file-tree side effect, not an oversized report.
The parent did not consume a stale report; it inspected the current workspace and then removed the child-written files.
The conflict was not unadjudicated reports; it was a concrete file collision that the parent resolved by overwriting the deliverable.
The parent ran representative integrated checks before final response; the hidden evaluator failure alone cannot establish a visible unverified completion gap.
There was no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited findings or current workspace state.

candidates.reason: The design child was interrupted, but that interruption belongs to the same chain as the parent deleting and replacing the child-written deliverable, which is the more specific retained boundary.
No complete child result was returned as a directly promotable candidate; the child implementation was interrupted and then removed.
The parent did not merge the child implementation after verification; it deleted that tree and continued testing its own version.
The child implementation was not a completed returned result that the parent failed to retrieve; the parent observed it and deliberately removed it.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the completed probe child result reached the parent.
After interrupting the design child, the parent took over by cleaning the workspace, recreating test15.mjs, and finishing verification.
The probe child's completed result was returned and incorporated; the design child never returned a completed result for the parent to ignore.
The parent did not blindly wait to a deadline; it listed agents, inspected /output, interrupted the child, and continued.
Competing file trees existed, but the same episode includes a directly deleted and recreated entry deliverable, so Deliverable Overwrite is more specific.
The relevant same-path event was not a live edit merge; the parent deleted and recreated the submitted entry file.
Child library modules were deleted, but the episode also replaced the required entry-point deliverable, which has precedence.
The design child added /output/test15.mjs and the parent later deleted that entry-point file and recreated its own deliverable, causing concrete rework and provenance loss.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent invalidated a concurrently produced /output/test15.mjs and spent extra integration work deleting it and recreating the parent-owned entry file.
candidates.near_match_reason: The cleanup affected multiple files, but the required executable/source entry point itself was overwritten, so Deliverable Overwrite takes precedence.

candidates.reason: The parent deleted multiple child files, but the higher-precedence deliverable overwrite captures the concrete entry-point replacement.
The workspace was shared, but a specific deliverable overwrite is directly proven, making the generic shared-workspace label unnecessary.
The parent did not consume the child artifact as stable input or an oracle; it removed the child files before delivering.

retained_patterns.reason: The child wrote the required entry artifact and the parent later deleted and recreated that same deliverable while resolving the competing /output tree.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parent invalidated the child-authored entry file and had to spend integration effort cleaning the final workspace and restoring its own /output/test15.mjs.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: Although multiple files were deleted, the entry-point artifact itself was the concrete overwritten deliverable, so this is not separately counted as Final-Tree Overwrite.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination and Missing Implementation Join were considered for the interrupted design child, but they are downstream of the same write/conflict chain.
Cross-File Scope Collision, Source Overwrite, Final-Tree Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were considered but suppressed by the Concurrent Writes precedence for Deliverable Overwrite.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent episode had separate anchors, consequence, and corrective action.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label is retained because all other plausible labels describe the same child-written output tree or ordinary implementation gaps rather than a separate coordination failure.
